scope: Independent read-only review of frozen A5 source, structural mesh sections, bed contact and downward surfaces. No CAD changes, UI, slicer, printer, or duplicate folding/access sweep.
provenance: Source and all four print STL hashes match CAD verification.json. No independent OpenSCAD regeneration performed.
architecture: One flat print containing three captive trays. Four integral opposed cone/divot A bearings at Y +/-30.5 mm. Only boards are installed afterward; no separate hinge pins/cartridges.
structural_observations: Most side edges are low base rims, not full-height sidewalls. Embedded bearing feet reinforce their local rim sections; the locally 1.4 mm lip is not a standalone tower.
Male posts and socket stem walls measure 3 mm between their outside surfaces and relieved arches. Relief roofs rise at 45 degrees; feet and cheek posts start at the print bed.
USB-end fixed lips and rear retaining catches have sloped undersides. All four PCB corner seats are rooted in the base; they contact bare PCB end strips rather than the glass.
Rear guards retain a broad main body and a low root into the base. At Y=-45.1,Z=1.5 the positive root spans X=23.935..29 (about5.065 mm). It merges into the solid end band by Y=-44.9.

The rounded forward end of each rear side guard is clipped by the bearing sweep pocket. Above the base its local tapered tip is about0.614 mm wide at Y=-44.4 and0.333 mm at Y=-44.2. This short edge remains attached to the broad guard; it is not an isolated wafer or the primary root. The slicer may simplify/omit its finest edge.

Horizontal latch beams have through-air isolation and rounded central root blends. Their practical free span is approximately17 mm, not the full22 mm drawn length. Guard geometry limits rear travel to0.9 mm.
unsupported_start_review: Each complete tray is one bed-contacting solid. Source inspection found no elevated disconnected starts; meaningful elevated horizontal underside area and elevated downward area beyond45 degrees are zero within stated mesh tolerance. This is geometric evidence, not slicer validation.
separate_CAD_validation_reference: CAD verification.json records362 shell/hardware fold poses,21 service/button checks at90/0/-90 degrees, released-latch insertion and travel checks. Those checks were not duplicated here.
limits: This A5 has not been physically printed, released, assembled with the actual boards, or load/fatigue/drop tested. Prior user preference for hinge A does not validate this new larger support architecture.

Geometric thickness/connectivity does not establish PLA strength, latch release force, elastic strain, fatigue or creep. The 17 mm beam and2 mm bending thickness still require a physical trial; the tall bearing supports carry lever loads.

Face-angle and bed-contact checks do not guarantee extrusion paths, pointed arch closure, small conical facets, cooling or support-free success. Inspect the slicer layers, including the tapered guard tips, before printing.
Actual printer calibration, first-layer spread and shrinkage can close the0.4 mm normal/0.5 mm axial hinge gaps. Release effort, wear and binding are unmeasured.

Connector/button positions and overmould/access envelopes remain approximate to the particular CYD variant. The CAD clearance results are not a measured fit guarantee. Side-port service uses the stated90/0/-90 pose.
USB plug clearance was checked in its modeled access pose. Folding with cables attached, cable bend radius and pinch protection are not established.
Low perimeter ribs reduce material and clear the hinge sweep, but provide less edge shielding than tall case walls. The screen seams remain determined by the physical board/glass geometry.
